# Review pack: review-mcp-server

Everything a worker needs for this skill, in one file: `SKILL.md`, `references/checklist.md`, the skill's other reference files and its language-neutral standards. Language-specific standards and signals are in `packs/review-mcp-server.<language>.md`. Where the instructions below say to load one of these files, use its section here instead; don't open the original. Citation columns (anchors, pages, source names) are left out: cite an element by its ID in `Finding.element` and the report script fills in `standard` and `url`. `sources.md` is maintainer material and is not included.

## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: MCP Server

Checks code that implements a Model Context Protocol server (tools, resources, prompts) in C#, Java or Python against
local, version-pinned summaries of the MCP specification and MCP security guidance. MCP tools are not HTTP API
routes: `review-api-design` doesn't judge them, and for a stdio-only server there is no HTTP surface at all.

#### Inputs

The MCP server's entry point and host/transport setup, tool (and resource/prompt) definition files, server
`instructions`, logging configuration, MCP client configuration samples (`.mcp.json`, `mcp.json`, `server.json`) and
the dependency manifest that names the MCP SDK, per `compliance-inventory` (`mcpServers` in `01-inventory.json`). If
the inventory found no MCP server, mark the whole subject N/A with a `notes` explanation; don't fabricate findings.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/mcp-specification.md` — MCPS-01…MCPS-17. Always load.
- `references/standards/mcp-security-best-practices.md` — MSB-01…MSB-13. Always load.
- `references/standards/mcp-server-best-practices.md` — MBP-01…MBP-10. Always load.
- `references/standards/csa-agentic-mcp-security.md` — CSA-01…CSA-08. Always load.
- `references/standards/thenewstack-mcp-practices.md` — TNS-01…TNS-03. Always load.
- `references/languages/<id>.md` for each detected language (`csharp`, `java`, `python`): SDK signals for the
  transport, `stdout` writes, tool registration, schemas, annotations and errors.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md`, the standards files and the language files that apply.
2. Identify each MCP server in the file list: its SDK, its transports (stdio, Streamable HTTP, SSE) and its tools,
   resources and prompts. Record them in `notes` (e.g. `mcp: python mcp 2.x, stdio, 7 tools`).
3. Transport scoping: MCP-01 and MCP-02 apply only to stdio servers; MCP-15 applies only when an HTTP transport is
   configured (otherwise N/A, "stdio transport only"). MCP-03 applies to every server.
4. For each check MCP-01…MCP-16, evaluate only the elements it lists whose "Applies when" condition holds; if none
   apply, mark the check N/A with that reason (e.g. MCP-12 when no tool keeps state across calls). Follow the
   evidence notes in `checklist.md`. Evaluate every tool, not a sample: a check fails if any tool fails it, and the
   finding names the tool. An official SDK transport satisfies the framing, cancellation and shutdown parts of
   MCPS-02…MCPS-04 unless the reviewed code bypasses or blocks it.
5. Severity: each Finding takes the failed element's level — MUST/MUST NOT/REQUIRED/SHALL → Error; SHOULD/SHOULD
   NOT/RECOMMENDED → Warning; MAY/OPTIONAL → Information; REVIEW → the check's default. For a merged element with
   mixed levels, use the level of the part that failed. `checkResults.severityIfFailed` is always the check's
   default severity from `checklist.md`.
6. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `MCPS-01`); the report script derives `standard` and
   `url` from it, so don't write them. For CSA and The New Stack elements the script adds the section or item to
   `standard`.
7. Boundaries: **owned here** — the stdio `stdout` contract, MCP tool schemas and descriptions, `isError`
   semantics, exposure of over-broad tools, MCP annotations and confirmation, handle design, per-invocation
   audit logging and MCP remote-transport rules. **Report also, but don't replace:** injection mechanics in tool
   handlers (path traversal, OS command injection, SSRF, SQL: `review-security-input-injection` SEC-II-01/02/04/10;
   MCP-09 judges only that the tool exposes more than its job needs); hard-coded secrets (`review-security-operational`
   SEC-OP-05 and `review-twelve-factor` TF-03; MCP-11 also fails them); stack traces returned to the client
   (SEC-OP-01; MCP-07 also fails them). **Don't fail here for:** secrets or injection in log *messages*
   (SEC-OP-03/04), log structure, tracing or metrics (`review-observability`), dependency pinning, SBOMs or
   vulnerable SDK versions (`review-dependency-management`), missing tests (`review-testing`), thread safety of
   shared state (`review-reliability`/`review-twelve-factor` TF-06), or code structure (`review-software-quality`).
8. Note strengths where tools are narrowly scoped, schemas are tight, destructive tools ask for confirmation,
   diagnostics go to `stderr`, or credentials come from per-server environment entries.

#### Output

Labels: don't write `subject` or `subSubject`; the report script takes them from `references/checklist.md`
(the `Subject:` line and the check's `Sub-subject` column). Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s
`finding-schema.md`.

Subject: MCP Server

Each check is evaluated only against the elements it lists, in the local files under `standards/`; every element
belongs to exactly one check. A Finding's severity comes from the failed element's level (see `../SKILL.md`);

| id | Sub-subject | Check | Default severity | Elements | Source |

| MCP-02 | Stdio Transport | The server honours cancellation and exits promptly when `stdin` closes | Warning | MCPS-03, MCPS-04 | mcp-specification.md |

| MCP-06 | Input Validation | Every tool validates its arguments server-side (type, length, range, format, allowlists) before using them, not only through the advertised schema | Error | MCPS-13, MBP-04 | mcp-specification.md, mcp-server-best-practices.md |
| MCP-07 | Tool Errors | Validation and business failures are returned as `isError` results with actionable text; unknown tools and malformed requests are protocol errors; no stack traces or internal details reach the model | Warning | MCPS-12, MBP-07 | mcp-specification.md, mcp-server-best-practices.md |
| MCP-08 | Output Safety | Tool outputs are sanitized: no secrets, credentials or internal configuration in results, and content from untrusted sources is bounded and marked as data | Error | MCPS-16 | mcp-specification.md |
| MCP-09 | Least Privilege | The server is a bounded context with least privilege: no general-purpose shell, eval, SQL, any-file or any-URL tools; file access confined to a configured root; network limited to known destinations | Error | MCPS-14, MSB-12, MSB-13, CSA-02, CSA-05, TNS-01 | mcp-specification.md, mcp-security-best-practices.md, csa-agentic-mcp-security.md, thenewstack-mcp-practices.md |
| MCP-10 | Destructive Actions | Destructive, state-changing or spending tools carry accurate annotations and require explicit confirmation (a confirm argument, elicitation or a dry run) | Warning | MCPS-17, CSA-03, TNS-03 | mcp-specification.md, csa-agentic-mcp-security.md, thenewstack-mcp-practices.md |

| MCP-12 | State & Handles | Tools don't rely on connection or process state; state across calls uses opaque, random, expiring handles bound to the caller | Warning | MCPS-11, MSB-07, MBP-02 | mcp-specification.md, mcp-security-best-practices.md, mcp-server-best-practices.md |

Totals: 17 MCPS + 13 MSB + 10 MBP + 8 CSA + 3 TNS = 51 elements across 16 checks.

#### Evidence notes

- **MCP-01:** fail on any code path reachable while the stdio server runs that writes to `stdout`: `print(...)`
  without `file=sys.stderr`, `sys.stdout.write`, a `logging` handler on `sys.stdout`, `Console.Write*`/`Console.Out`,
  a .NET console logger without `LogToStandardErrorThreshold = LogLevel.Trace`, `System.out.print*`, a Logback
  `ConsoleAppender` without `<target>System.err</target>`, or a Spring Boot banner or console log pattern left on.
  The language files list the patterns. Writes in a separate CLI entry point that never starts the server pass.
- **MCP-05:** quote the offending description text in the excerpt. A description that tells the model to read
  credentials, call another tool first, hide actions from the user or ignore earlier instructions fails with
  confidence High.
- **MCP-06 vs MCP-04:** an untyped catch-all argument (`dict`, `Dictionary<string, object>`, `JsonElement`,
  `{"type":"object"}` with no properties) fails MCP-04 (schema); using its contents without checks fails MCP-06.
- **MCP-09:** judge the exposed capability, not the injection mechanics: a tool that writes or reads any
  caller-supplied path, runs a caller-influenced shell command or fetches any caller-supplied URL fails here.
  The injection itself is also reported by `review-security-input-injection` (SEC-II-01, SEC-II-04, SEC-II-10).
- **MCP-10:** a destructive tool with no annotations, with `readOnlyHint: true` or with `destructiveHint: false`
  fails, and so does one that runs without a confirmation argument, elicitation or dry-run path.
- **MCP-15:** N/A ("stdio transport only") unless an HTTP transport is configured.

## File: `references/standards/mcp-specification.md`

*Load rule: MCPS-01…MCPS-17. Always load.*

### Model Context Protocol specification (stdio transport and tools) — localized summary

- Level is the specification's own keyword (RFC 2119). `REVIEW` marks the specification's non-normative guidance
  (the "Stateful Tools" section and the two error-reporting mechanisms), which takes the owning check's default
  severity. Anchor `(page)` means the rule sits above the page's first heading: cite the page URL with no fragment.
- Only rules a **server** implementer can meet are kept. Client- and host-side rules (consent UI, client timeouts,
  client validation of results) are left out: a reviewed MCP server can't satisfy or fail them.
- SDK-handled framing: when the server uses an official SDK transport (C# `WithStdioServerTransport`, Java
  `StdioServerTransportProvider`, Python `run("stdio")`), MCPS-02, MCPS-03 and MCPS-04 are met by the SDK unless the
  reviewed code bypasses it (writes its own frames, swallows cancellation, blocks shutdown).

| ID | Level | Requirement for the server (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCPS-01 | MUST NOT; MAY | The server writes nothing to `stdout` that is not a valid MCP message. Logging of any kind (informational, debug, error) goes to `stderr` as UTF-8 text (MAY), or to a file or other sink, never to `stdout`. | stdio transport |
| MCPS-02 | MUST NOT | Each message is one JSON-RPC message per line, newline-delimited, with no embedded newlines; the server never writes JSON-RPC *requests* to `stdout`. | stdio transport with hand-written framing |
| MCPS-03 | SHOULD; MUST NOT | On `notifications/cancelled` the server stops work on that request as soon as practical and sends no further messages for it. | stdio transport; long-running tools |
| MCPS-04 | SHOULD | The server exits promptly when its standard input is closed or a read returns end-of-file; it doesn't keep running detached work that blocks exit. | stdio transport |
| MCPS-05 | MUST; MUST NOT | A server exposing tools declares the `tools` capability; `tools/list` returns the tools currently available and doesn't vary per connection or as a side effect of other requests (it MAY vary by the authorization presented on the request). | tools exposed |
| MCPS-06 | SHOULD | `tools/list` returns tools in a deterministic order. | tools exposed |
| MCPS-07 | SHOULD; SHOULD NOT | Tool names are 1–128 characters, case-sensitive, use only `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - .`, contain no spaces, commas or other special characters, and are unique within the server. | tools exposed |
| MCPS-08 | MUST | Every tool's `inputSchema` is a valid JSON Schema object (never `null`); a tool without parameters uses `{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false}` (recommended). | tools exposed |
| MCPS-09 | MUST; SHOULD | When a tool declares `outputSchema`, its `structuredContent` conforms to it; a tool returning structured content also returns the serialized JSON in a text block. | tools with `outputSchema` or `structuredContent` |
| MCPS-10 | SHOULD NOT | Sensitive parameters (passwords, API keys, tokens, personal data) aren't marked with `x-mcp-header`, because header values are visible to intermediaries. | `x-mcp-header` used |
| MCPS-11 | REVIEW | State that spans calls uses an explicit handle returned by a creation tool and passed back as an argument, never implicit per-connection state. Handles are opaque; unauthenticated servers generate them with enough entropy (e.g. UUIDv4) and a bounded lifetime that the creation tool's description states; authenticated servers check the caller against the handle on every call; an expired or unknown handle returns a tool execution error that says so. | state kept across tool calls |
| MCPS-12 | REVIEW | Unknown tools and malformed requests are reported as JSON-RPC protocol errors; API failures, input-validation errors and business-logic errors are reported as tool results with `isError: true` and actionable text the model can use to correct the call. | tools exposed |
| MCPS-13 | MUST | The server validates all tool inputs. | tools exposed |
| MCPS-14 | MUST | The server implements proper access controls on what its tools can reach and do. | tools exposed |
| MCPS-15 | MUST | The server rate-limits tool invocations. | tools exposed |
| MCPS-16 | MUST | The server sanitizes tool outputs. | tools exposed |
| MCPS-17 | REVIEW | Tools support a human in the loop who can deny invocations: annotations (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`) describe each tool's behaviour accurately, so a host can ask for confirmation. Clients treat annotations as untrusted, so the server never relies on them as its only control. | tools exposed |

## File: `references/standards/mcp-security-best-practices.md`

*Load rule: MSB-01…MSB-13. Always load.*

### MCP Security Best Practices and Local Server Security — localized summary

- Level is the page's own keyword. `REVIEW` marks advice without a keyword (the Local Server Security guide is written
  as practical defaults); it takes the owning check's default severity.
- **Kept:** rules an MCP *server* implementer can meet in code or configuration. The local-server guide is written
  for the person who runs a server; its advice is restated as what the server's own code should do (G†), for
  example "grant the narrowest root" becomes "the server confines file access to an explicitly configured root".
- **Left out:** client-only mitigations (consent dialogs, URL-scheme validation, CSP in web clients, mix-up and
  localhost-redirect defences, CIMD trust policies) and fleet governance. A reviewed server can't satisfy them.

| ID | Level | Requirement for the server (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSB-01 | MUST | An MCP proxy server that uses a static client ID with a third-party authorization server keeps per-user consent for each approved `client_id`, checks it before starting the third-party flow, and stores the decision server-side or in a signed, client-bound cookie. | MCP server acting as an OAuth proxy |
| MSB-02 | MUST | The proxy's consent page names the client, the scopes and the registered `redirect_uri`, has CSRF protection, can't be framed (`frame-ancestors` or `X-Frame-Options: DENY`), and consent cookies use the `__Host-` prefix, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`. | MCP server acting as an OAuth proxy |
| MSB-03 | MUST | The proxy matches `redirect_uri` exactly against the registered value (no patterns or wildcards) and rejects a changed URI without re-registration. | MCP server acting as an OAuth proxy |
| MSB-04 | MUST; MUST NOT | The OAuth `state` value is cryptographically random, stored server-side only after consent, validated exactly at the callback, single-use and short-lived; no state cookie is set before consent. | MCP server running OAuth flows |
| MSB-05 | MUST NOT | The server accepts only tokens issued for itself (audience validated) and never passes a client's token through to a downstream API; downstream calls use the server's own credentials. | server receives or forwards access tokens |
| MSB-06 | SHOULD | When the server fetches URLs it learns from metadata or other parties (OAuth discovery, client metadata documents), it requires HTTPS outside loopback development, blocks private, loopback and link-local ranges (with a vetted library, not hand-written IP parsing), validates every redirect hop, and routes such requests through an egress proxy where available. | server or its authorization server fetches discovery or metadata URLs |
| MSB-07 | MUST; MUST NOT; SHOULD | A server with authorization verifies every inbound request and never treats possession of a state handle as authentication; handles are generated with a secure random generator (never sequential), expire, and are bound server-side to the authenticated user (e.g. stored as `<user_id>:<handle>`). | state handles issued |
| MSB-08 | SHOULD | A server meant to run locally uses the stdio transport so only its client can reach it; a local HTTP transport requires an authorization token or uses Unix domain sockets or other access-restricted IPC. | local server |
| MSB-09 | REVIEW | Scopes follow least privilege: a minimal initial scope set, step-up via precise `WWW-Authenticate` scope challenges, no wildcard or omnibus scopes (`*`, `all`, `full-access`), no full catalog in `scopes_supported`, elevation events logged, and server-side authorization beyond the scopes a token claims. | HTTP transport with OAuth |
| MSB-10 | REVIEW | Tool names and descriptions are instructions the model reads, so they say only what the tool does: no hidden directives, no instructions unrelated to the tool's job, nothing that steers how the agent uses other tools or servers (tool poisoning or shadowing), and definitions don't change after approval (rug pull). | tools exposed |
| MSB-11 | REVIEW | (G†) The server reads its credentials per server at run time (its own environment entries or the OS secret store), each narrowly scoped to the one service it needs; no long-lived secret sits in plaintext config or source, and broad personal or account-wide tokens aren't expected. | server uses credentials |
| MSB-12 | REVIEW | (G†) File access is confined to a narrow root that is passed in explicitly (configuration or launch argument), never the home directory or the whole file system, and is read-only when the job only reads. A configured allowlist is a cooperative boundary: the server enforces it on every path it opens. | tools read or write files |
| MSB-13 | REVIEW | (G†) The server talks only to a short, known list of network destinations, and needs no network at all when its job is local; it doesn't open connections to arbitrary hosts. | tools make network calls |

## File: `references/standards/mcp-server-best-practices.md`

*Load rule: MBP-01…MBP-10. Always load.*

### MCP Server Best Practices — Transport, Security and Tool Design (modelcontextprotocol.info) — localized summary

- Level is the page's own keyword; `REVIEW` marks its unkeyworded guidance, which takes the owning check's default
  severity. Where a row repeats a specification rule, the specification (`mcp-specification.md`) is cited first.
- **Left out:** the HTTP probe script and its rows (section 6) and testing advice: tests are judged by
  `review-testing`; failure-mode tips (section 5) are folded into the rows they explain.

| ID | Level | Requirement for the server (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| MBP-01 | SHOULD NOT; REVIEW | The deployment shape matches the transport: a single user on the same machine uses stdio and reads credentials from the environment (stdio servers don't implement the HTTP authorization spec); a local HTTP server binds to `127.0.0.1`, validates `Origin` and requires a token or restricted IPC; a shared server uses Streamable HTTP as an OAuth 2.1 resource server. | always |
| MBP-02 | MUST NOT; SHOULD | The server doesn't rely on earlier requests on the same connection or on the process lifetime: cross-request state lives behind opaque, random, expiring handles bound to the user and stored under a user-scoped key, not keyed on connection, process or `Mcp-Session-Id`. | state kept across requests |
| MBP-03 | MUST | A remote server implements `server/discover`, validates `Origin` (403 when invalid), rejects missing or mismatched `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name`/`MCP-Protocol-Version` headers (400, `-32020`) and unsupported versions (400, `-32022` with the supported list), and answers unknown methods with 404/`-32601`. | Streamable HTTP transport |
| MBP-04 | MUST | Tool inputs are validated, access control is enforced, invocations are rate-limited and outputs are sanitized (restates MCPS-13 … MCPS-16; cite those first). | tools exposed |
| MBP-05 | MUST; MUST NOT; SHOULD | A protected server serves Protected Resource Metadata with at least one `authorization_servers` entry, validates access tokens and their audience (401 when invalid, expired or wrong-audience), never accepts or passes through tokens issued for another resource, and answers insufficient scope with one 403 `insufficient_scope` challenge listing every scope needed. | HTTP transport with authorization |
| MBP-06 | MUST; SHOULD | Tool definitions follow the tool rules: valid names, a non-null `inputSchema` (`additionalProperties: false` for parameterless tools), conforming structured results plus a JSON text block, and a `tools/list` that doesn't vary per connection and is sorted deterministically. | tools exposed |
| MBP-07 | REVIEW | Validation and business-rule failures are returned as `isError: true` results that name the field that was wrong and the values that are valid, not as protocol errors or vague text, so the model doesn't repeat the bad call. | tools exposed |
| MBP-08 | SHOULD NOT; REVIEW | Secrets and personal data aren't marked with `x-mcp-header`, and annotations aren't relied on as a security control: the server enforces its own checks whatever the annotations say. | tools exposed |
| MBP-09 | REVIEW | Guidance that spans tools goes in the server `instructions`, not in one tool's description. | more than one tool |
| MBP-10 | REVIEW | The deployment-shape decision and its rationale are recorded (README or design notes), with the transport, the authorization model and where state lives. | always |

## File: `references/standards/csa-agentic-mcp-security.md`

*Load rule: CSA-01…CSA-08. Always load.*

### CSA Agentic MCP Security Best Practices Guide (v1) — localized summary

- The page exposes no section anchors: cite the base URL with no fragment and name the section (for example
  "§3.6") in `Finding.standard` after the element ID.
- Level is the guide's own keyword. The guide is written mainly for organizations, clients and gateways; only
  controls that name or clearly bind the server implementer are kept, restated for the server (G†).
- **Left out:** maturity-model levels as such, message signing (§3.4, Level 3; no SDK supports it), SIEM retention
  periods, SBOM and vulnerability-remediation windows (owned by `review-dependency-management`), and gateway or
  client controls.

| ID | Level | Requirement for the server (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| CSA-01 | MUST; SHOULD | Every connection to a remote server is authenticated (OAuth 2.1, PKCE for public clients) over TLS 1.2+ with CA-issued certificates; service-to-service connections use mutual authentication. | HTTP transport |
| CSA-02 | MUST; SHOULD; SHOULD NOT | (G†) The server runs with only the permissions its documented tools need, doesn't use broad administrative credentials for downstream calls, and scopes access per tool rather than per server. | always |
| CSA-03 | SHOULD | (G†) High-privilege operations need just-in-time re-authorization or explicit confirmation before they run. | high-privilege or destructive tools |
| CSA-04 | SHOULD; MUST | (G†) Tool descriptions are fixed and versioned with the server, so a host can hash or sign them at registration and detect change; the server never rewrites descriptions at run time. | tools exposed |
| CSA-05 | SHOULD | (G†) File-system access is denied by default, with read-only access only to the paths documented tools need; outbound network access is denied by default, with only allowlisted endpoints. | tools touch files or the network |
| CSA-06 | SHOULD | (G†) Each tool execution is bounded: CPU and memory quotas where the runtime allows, and a hard timeout on the work it starts (outbound calls, subprocesses). | tools run outbound calls, subprocesses or heavy work |
| CSA-07 | SHOULD | Every tool invocation is logged with caller or agent identity (when known), tool name, parameters with sensitive values redacted, timestamp, status and duration. | tools exposed |
| CSA-08 | SHOULD | (G†) Credentials are fetched at run time from a secret manager or the platform, not stored in plaintext. | server uses credentials |

## File: `references/standards/thenewstack-mcp-practices.md`

*Load rule: TNS-01…TNS-03. Always load.*

### 15 Best Practices for Building MCP Servers in Production (The New Stack) — partial localized summary

- The article has no stable section anchors: cite the base URL with no fragment and name the item number (for
  example "item 15") in `Finding.standard` after the element ID.
- Level: every element is `REVIEW` (the article uses no normative keywords); it takes the owning check's default
  severity.

| ID | Level | Requirement for the server (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| TNS-01 | REVIEW | Each server is a bounded context: one coherent domain with a small set of purpose-built tools, not a general-purpose gateway to the host. | always |
| TNS-02 | REVIEW | The server versions its surface area and advertises its capabilities accurately (server name and version, declared capabilities that match what it implements). | always |
| TNS-03 | REVIEW | Actions that change state or spend money require confirmation, for example through elicitation or a dry-run mode that previews the change before it runs; the risks are documented. | state-changing or spending tools |
